title: Minimum Cost to Divide Array Into Subarrays
summary: Given integer arrays nums and cost of equal length, and an integer k, find the minimum total cost by dividing nums into subarrays.
statement: Given integer arrays nums and cost of equal length, and an integer k, find the minimum total cost by dividing nums into subarrays. The cost of the i-th subarray is the sum of its elements plus k times i, multiplied by the sum of corresponding cost elements. The cost index i starts at 1.
constraints: nums and cost have equal length up to 1,000 and contain positive integers; k is positive.
For partition number q ending at r, cost is (prefix_nums[r]+k*q) times that segment’s cost sum.
Partition the full array into nonempty contiguous subarrays and minimize total cost.
hints: The order-dependent k term can be telescoped into a fixed k*total_cost charge per segment boundary.
Rewrite the DP transition as a line minimum with slope -prefix_cost at increasing x=prefix_nums+k.
Query the monotone hull, add prefix_nums*prefix_cost+k*total_cost, then insert the new decreasing-slope line.
Telescoping reproduces every partition index contribution, and monotone slopes/queries make deque convex-hull optimization exact.
editorial: Telescoping reproduces every partition index contribution, and monotone slopes/queries make deque convex-hull optimization exact.
